To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the periodicity of RNA discharge, in the cat, is not altered by chemoreceptor stimulation and is not dependent upon peripheral chemoreceptor input.

the 10 c/min rhythm of renal sympathetic nerve discharges is not dependent on the baroreceptor and peripheral chemo-receptor reflexes and that the periodicity of the 10 c/ min rhythm is not dependent on chemoreceptor reflexes.

chemoreceptor activation does not affect the fundamental 10 c/s rhythm and the stability and proportion of Tc and TB modes of RNA, but can alter the overall amplitude of synchronized bursts and interact with baroreceptors to increase RNA activity at high blood pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the periodicity of the synchronized renal sympathetic nerve discharge in the cat.
the neural control of the renal circulation in the conscious and anesthetized animal.
the mechanisms that generate periodicity of renal nerve activity and how they are affected by the autonomic nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemoreceptor system does not appear to play a significant role in the control of RNA periodicity.
the periodicities of RNA are not altered by chemoreceptor stimulation but the overall amplitude and number of active fibers are increased.
the fundamental periodicity is not altered by chemoreceptor stimulation but the number of active renal nerve fibres is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the periodicity of the fundamental rhythm is maintained by a central pacemaker, which is not influenced by peripheral chemoreceptors.
the fundamental periodicity of the sympathetic nerve activity is generated in the central nervous system and is not altered by chemoreceptor or baroreflex stimulation.
the fundamental rhythm of RNA is generated by a central pacemaker, and is modulated by afferent information to the brainstem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fundamental rhythm is a stable feature of the sympathetic nervous system, which is not altered by chemoreceptor stimulation.
the periodicity of RNA does not appear to be influenced by chemoreceptor activation.
chemoreceptor activation does not change the fundamental rhythm of RNA.
